pillar_reactions.evidence: He had already been running Trevor's free content for a week and volunteered an unprompted result: 'I noticed a difference in a week, dude... the other day I was walking down the street to grab coffee... my shoulders were just naturally sitting broadly, and they just felt really good... I had like a big cheesy smile on my face because I was like, my shoulders actually feel good.' When the mobility-as-foundation pillar was presented he tied it straight to his own history: 'it aligns so well because it kind of makes me want to retract something that I may have said... For the longest time, all I did was lifting weights. And before I knew it, I noticed that I was really stiff.'

The pitch landed directly on his live grievance. He had just described a nutritionist prescribing protein bars and protein chips, and the rep's framing was 'So we're not eating. Protein chips. We focus on micronutrients' and 'no laborious, tedious macro counting'. His stated want, minutes earlier, had been almost word for word the same: 'I don't want to have to worry about, oh, like, I got to write down my macros and it's like this mathematical equation every time I prepare a meal.' Response: 'It does, 100%.'

Presented as 24/7 Trevor access, form-clip review, weekly check-ins with tracking, and being held to 'the guy who feels healthy, feels good, super consistent'. His response was the sharpest question anyone asks in this batch, and it was about whether any of it would actually deliver: 'what expectations should I have? Right? I've been unhappy with, you know, this current nutritional program, and I haven't figured out for the life of me if I have higher expectations than I should.' He accepted the answer he was given but the question was about proof, not mechanics.

anchors.raw: I've been paying $200 a month for, for the past two months, and it's a three-month program... I thought $600 across three months was a lot for a nutritional program, right?
anchors.note: The dominant anchor and a double one. It sets his reference price for paid coaching at $600 total, against which $6,000 is ten times, and he made the comparison himself at the exact moment he declined. It also carries a trust wound — he calls it 'kind of a scam' — so the anchor does not just undercut on price, it primes him to expect not to get value. The rep worked the trust half skilfully and never touched the price half.

anchors.raw: in fact, for the past week, I've been training using Trevor's content... I noticed a difference in a week, dude, like, like legit in a week
anchors.note: The most awkward anchor in the corpus so far: the company's own free content had already produced a felt result in seven days. It is powerful proof of the modality and simultaneously the strongest argument for not paying $6,000 — he is getting posture changes for nothing. It was never addressed. The unstated answer is programming, progression and the form-review loop, and nobody said it.

anchors.raw: I had someone else's content that I was following. His name is Thomas DeLauer. He's actually on YouTube as well. But I lost over 60 pounds following Keto.
anchors.note: He has already produced the single biggest result of his life — 60 to 70 lb — from free content and his own discipline. That is a genuine, demonstrated, zero-cost substitute. It also self-destructed after eighteen months, which is precisely the sustainability argument the offer is built on, but the rep only referenced keto in passing as 'super restrictive' rather than making it the case for the purchase.

anchors.raw: with a pay increase, I can finally go back to just one job, and spending 6k makes me feel like I have to go back to a second job again, and I just can't do that
anchors.note: Not really an anchor about fitness at all — it is the thing he is actually buying with the pay rise, which is the end of a second job. The purchase was perceived as reversing the exact benefit he had just secured. The rep answered this with an interpretation reframe rather than with arithmetic, and then offered a plan that raises the total, which sharpens rather than resolves the conflict.

anchors.raw: I've ordered 20-pound kettlebells, a set, should be having those soon
anchors.note: He has already bought the equipment and is training on it. Modality risk is zero and the switching cost of walking away is real. Combined with the declared belief — 'Yes, I have no doubt' — the only live obstacle on this call is the number.

unmet_demand.want: An instalment structure that spreads the cost monthly without increasing it
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only interest-free option is 50% down with the balance inside 90 days, which is not monthly and still requires $3,000 immediately. Everything genuinely monthly costs more: the internal 12-month route is $650 x 12 = $7,800, and Klarna declined him twice. A prospect with real intent, declared belief and constrained liquidity had no route he could both afford and accept. This is a commercial product gap, not a rep failure.

unmet_demand.want: A clear statement of what results to expect, given he had just been burned by a paid programme — 'what expectations should I have?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The answer he was given was the guarantee: an eight-kilo increase on every kettlebell movement in six months. That measures load progression. None of his actual goals are load progression — he wants the belly fat gone, energy back, the hip pain fixed and to stop feeling fifty. The guarantee is real and tangible but it is denominated in the wrong currency for this buyer, and nobody bridged it to his outcomes.

unmet_demand.want: Kettlebell training that survives a flight attendant roster with no fixed days and layover hotel gyms that have no kettlebells
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Actually solved on the call, and solved well — the rep restructured to two kettlebell days plus two equipment-free calisthenics days and used his own EMOM session that morning as the example. Recorded because it was the prospect's first stated hesitation about the programme and the resolution was one of the strongest moments in the call.
